summary: Content farms uploaded videos with sexually graphic bestiality-themed thumbnails that slipped past YouTube's moderation and were surfaced by its recommendation engine, drawing millions of views. YouTube removed the content after journalists flagged it.
technical_summary: YouTube's automated thumbnail and content moderation checked video content but not graphic thumbnails. Content farms exploited this gap with clickbait thumbnails to inflate views and ad revenue, and the recommendation engine then amplified the videos to users.

summary: Google Photos' automatic image labeling tagged photos of two Black people as 'gorillas'. Google apologized and later removed gorilla and some other primate labels from the service.
technical_summary: Google Photos used machine-learning image recognition to auto-tag and group photos. The classifier mislabeled images of Black people as gorillas, reflecting weak performance on darker-skinned faces. Google's fix was to block the gorilla label and search terms rather than retrain.

summary: A lawsuit alleges that Amazon's AI-assisted driver monitoring pushed delivery drivers to put speed ahead of safety, contributing to a delivery van crash that left a passenger in another car with life-changing injuries. Amazon denies liability.
technical_summary: Amazon monitors delivery drivers through a phone app, van sensors and AI cameras that track speed, braking, cornering, phone use and yawning. The lawsuit alleges this system and associated delivery targets pressured drivers toward unsafe speed, leading to a rear-end collision on an interstate.

summary: In an ACLU test, Amazon's Rekognition face-matching tool wrongly matched 28 members of Congress to arrest mugshots, with people of color disproportionately affected. No one was actually detained as a result of the test.
technical_summary: The ACLU built a face database from 25,000 public arrest photos and searched it with Rekognition at default settings against photos of all members of Congress. The system returned false matches, with nearly 40 percent involving people of color, showing unequal accuracy across groups.

technical_summary: A synthetic video, with altered speech and a sombrero and mustache added to one figure, was published on a social platform by a political actor. The generation tool is unidentified. The clip put false claims in a real politician's mouth to mock opponents amid budget negotiations.

summary: Brazil's labor-court AI tool Galileu detected hidden instructions in a legal petition that tried to make it contest the case superficially. It alerted the judge and blocked the hidden text, and a human reviewed the matter.
technical_summary: A petition contained hidden text addressed to the court's AI assistant, a prompt injection instructing it to weakly contest the filing and not challenge documents. Galileu detected the embedded instructions, warned the user, and refused to process them, leaving the judge to review and decide on consequences.

summary: US auto-safety regulators linked Tesla's Autopilot to at least 13 fatal crashes and hundreds of other crashes, and opened a new probe into whether Tesla's December recall of about 2 million vehicles was adequate.
technical_summary: Autopilot is a driver-assist system. NHTSA found its weak driver-engagement safeguards did not match its permissive operating capabilities, and that its name and design invited over-trust. Drivers missed visible hazards, producing avoidable crashes, some after the recall software update.
